reuse.why: The tree already had getScheduledAmount deciding missing/number/range; the diff adds a parallel getPlannedAmount for server sites and bolts a positional op argument onto getScheduledAmount for UI sites, instead of evolving the one existing helper.

duplication.why: Most midpoint copies are replaced by a shared call, but computeSchedulePreviewTransactions keeps its own missing/number/range dispatch (now calling getRangeAmount), duplicating getPlannedAmount's dispatch.

placement.why: The amount rule lives in shared/schedules.ts, reusing the approx threshold from shared/rules; the API model calls it in the mapper layer.

scope.why: Focused on the four steps, though the step-1 release note still describes the superseded 'furthest from zero' rule.

maintainability.why: Two entry points (getScheduledAmount(amount, false, op) and getPlannedAmount(amount, op)) for the same decision plus one site with its own dispatch that ignores approximate amounts invite divergence.

bypasses_abstraction.where: shared/schedules.ts computeSchedulePreviewTransactions keeps an inline null/number/range ternary and calls only getRangeAmount, bypassing getPlannedAmount/getScheduledAmount (so approximate amounts are not planned there).

disguised_duplication.where: computeSchedulePreviewTransactions' inline dispatch reshapes getPlannedAmount's missing/number/range logic around getRangeAmount instead of calling the shared function.

abstraction_drift.where: getScheduledAmount gains a positional op parameter after the inverse boolean (callers pass false, op); getPlannedAmount adds an isapprox branch; computeSchedulePreviewTransactions bypasses both with its own dispatch.
